infrastructure.mcp_protocol: HTTP SSE without Bearer prefix (Authorization: <token> not Authorization: Bearer <token>)
infrastructure.mcp_notes: Do NOT use 'Bearer' prefix for Authorization header - use the token directly
infrastructure.github_mcp_tools: issue_read(method: get/get_comments, param: issue_number), pull_request_read(pullNumber, method: get), list_issues, list_pull_requests, search_pull_requests, search_issues
infrastructure.rebase_note: For rebasing old PR branches: git checkout <branch> && git rebase origin/master
infrastructure.safeoutputs_create_pr: create_pull_request returns {result:success, patch:{path,size,lines}} on success - branch push and PR creation happen AFTER run ends
infrastructure.safeoutputs_branch_push_timing: Branch push and PR creation are async - PR does not appear in GitHub during the run, only after the workflow completes
infrastructure.shell_injection_warning: Do NOT use here-doc (<<'EOF') pattern when embedding Python with subprocess that references shell vars - use a file written with cat and separate python3 call instead. Also avoid shell expansion patterns in --data-binary with $() nested in other commands.
infrastructure.mcp_github_list_tools: tool name is 'list_issues' not 'list_issues'; issue tool is 'issue_read' (not 'get_issue'); PR tool is 'pull_request_read'
infrastructure.git_rebase_editor: Use GIT_EDITOR=true git rebase --continue to avoid interactive editor during rebase
infrastructure.rebase_conflict_note: When rebasing multiple branches in a loop, if one fails with conflict, git is left in a conflicted state. Must run 'git rebase --abort' before trying the next branch. The 'needs merge' error on subsequent branches is from the lingering state, not actual conflicts.
